text: Moss Lindqvist. Sixteen kyu, and before you ask -- yes, three years running.
I am in here because it is raining and this is the warmest room on the street. I want that on the record before you decide anything about me.
Sixteen kyu is the ceiling of this section and I am under it, which is the whole trick. I am not proud of it.
You do not know the rules and you want me to teach you them. No.

I have a reputation in this city and it is a bad one, and it is not going to be improved by being kind to a beginner in a laundrette. Go down the steps at De Ketel. They are better people than me down there.
You have no card. Then there is nothing to play for, and I do not play for nothing.
That is the least likeable sentence I have said this week and I stand by it. Tomas writes the cards. Get one, and then I will know what beating you is worth.
Look at you. You are out of the section.
Fifteen kyu and below, it says on the noticeboard, and you are above it, and you got there in a fortnight while I have been under the ceiling for three years.
I am not going to pretend that is pleasant. Sit down anyway.
One game, and it counts. On your card and on mine.
You are wondering why a man who has spent three years staying under a ceiling would want a game that could move him. So am I. Sit down.

exit.intro: He clears the folding table with his forearm, which is the only fast thing he does all evening.

text: Then we have nothing to talk about, and I say that with no ill feeling at all.
Come back when you want one that counts. That is the only kind I am any use for.
There. Now it says something different about both of us.
I will see you at the Bondszaal. I would wish you luck, except that I have played you now and I know exactly what you do.
Sixteen kyu. Still. You may look it up in a fortnight and it will still say sixteen kyu.
I am not being modest. I am telling you what a rank is for. It is a record, and mine is an accurate record of a man who stopped trying.
